acceptance_criteria.criterion: GET /api/config/notes-display returns JSON { notesCardHeight: number, notesColumns: number } with current appConfig values
PUT /api/config/notes-display validates notesCardHeight as integer in range [120, 800] using constants from config.constants.ts
PUT /api/config/notes-display validates notesColumns as integer in range [1, 6] using constants from config.constants.ts
PUT /api/config/notes-display accepts partial updates — only provided fields are modified
PUT mutates in-memory appConfig and persists each changed field via saveConfigField()
PUT returns 400 with descriptive error message for invalid input (non-integer, out of range, non-number)
PUT returns the full current notes-display settings object on success

comments.note: The PUT /api/config/polling handler (config.ts ~line 259) splits integer validation into two separate conditions (isFinite then isInteger). The notes-display PUT follows the same pattern for consistency. A small helper like `isValidFiniteInteger(n)` could reduce the repeated guard pattern across polling, notesCardHeight, and notesColumns handlers — worth extracting if more integer-validated fields are added.

The existing route handlers in config.ts each repeat the three-step body-parse pattern (try/catch parseJsonBody → isPlainObject check → field extraction). This is a well-established local convention and remains consistent in the new notes-display PUT handler. No action needed unless the file grows further.

config.test.ts line 1091: Replaced over-engineered tri-clause assertion (!Object.hasOwn(...) || === undefined || === 2) with a single precise assertion (!Object.hasOwn(saved, 'notesColumns')). The original was logically correct but harder to read and carried a loose fallback (=== 2) that would pass even if the field were incorrectly written with the original value. The tighter form accurately captures the intent: a field that was never passed in a partial update should not appear in the config file at all. Non-behavioral — 808/808 tests pass.

[documentation-forward] The JSDoc table in registerConfigRoutes (config.ts lines 100–105) documents the two new endpoints but does not mention the partial-update semantics or the accepted field names/ranges for PUT /api/config/notes-display. Adding a brief note (e.g. 'Fields: notesCardHeight ∈ [120, 800], notesColumns ∈ [1, 6]; all fields optional') would make the table self-sufficient for future contributors without needing to read the handler body.
